A local workspace for writers

Revise your manuscript.
Keep the research in reach.

Where does the rhythm change? Which words repeat? Lixity takes you to the passage. Compare drafts and keep character dossiers and sources beside your text. The open-source app reads Markdown and plain-text files locally.

Try a sample passage → Watch the product tour ↓

A short practice exercise in English. Edit the sample in your browser.

From a marked passage to the next revision

Read, write, and check what changes in the text. Built-in analysis runs offline. Optional speech, map services, and connected AI clients have their own network and data-handling requirements.

Revise without losing your place

Keep your review marks by the text as you write with local autosave. Compare the draft with the saved manuscript under the same analysis settings before applying it.

Editor scope and availability (English)

See why the text was marked

Open a note about sentence rhythm, quotations, or repeated words and inspect the counted text. Compare chapters and follow available evidence back to the prose to decide what deserves a closer read.

Inspect a marked sentenceHow Lixity measures text

Follow a character through the manuscript

Draft a dossier from the prose and review its chapter distribution and passages in context. Keep your notes, claims, and exact source quotations beside the text.

Research, dossiers and evidence (English)

Share the version you checked

Download the selected dossier version as an A4 PDF with its saved notes, tables, excerpts, and source quotations. For the manuscript, choose a print layout or prepare a reading website with chapter limits and spoiler controls.

Inspect the signal. Make your own decision.

Measurements describe patterns in the supplied text. They do not grade literary quality or tell you how to rewrite a passage. Inspect the counted words and sentences, read them in context, and decide whether a difference matters.

Before you try Lixity

What does Lixity highlight?

Review sentence lengths, recognized quotations and repeated words in a paragraph, then compare chapters. Open a mark to see what was counted.

Where does my manuscript stay?

Built-in analysis runs on your computer, where your project files are stored. Optional services such as map providers and external language models have their own data requirements.

What can I try before installing?

Edit a paragraph in the browser exercise, which uses simplified rules. The English demo is a larger read-only example project. Install Lixity for full analysis and your own projects.

Bring your own manuscript.

Choose the setup for Windows, macOS or Linux. The guide takes you from installation to opening your manuscript.

Downloads and setup

The published browser app is available on PyPI. The demo and source guides describe development version v0.9.1.

Website measurement (English)

This public website uses GoatCounter to count page visits and named demo, installation, repository and PDF links. The adapter sends public page paths and event names, excluding query strings, fragments, form contents and manuscript selections. The local app and exported manuscript reports contain no such measurement.

Language and appearance choices are stored locally in this browser when storage is available. Browser language is used only to suggest a public introduction; it is not sent to a translation service or used to change manuscript analysis.

Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control disable collection. Counts are approximate and do not establish installations or active authors. GoatCounter receives technical request data; see its privacy information. For questions, use the contact below.
